newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish quiet day mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish quiet day mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished mixed, with September Standard and Poor's 500 futures lower in quiet trading.
Stock index futures tracked Treasury bonds lower in midday and afternoon trading, with September S&Ps slipping into neagtive territory. Traders cited a disappointing five-year note auction.
"It was dead quiet in here," an S&P trader said. "The auction was weak and they broke the bonds down to 108-20/32," pressuring stocks in turn, he said.
September S&Ps rose to a session high of 668.15, but drfited lower for the rest of the session. Near midday, two waves of sell programs were noted as the cash-futures spread narrowed.
Resistance was seen at 669.00, 669.25 and 671.30, traders said. Support was at 664.20 to 664.40.
The economic line-up was empty on Wednesday, but the latest weekly jobless claims, second-quarter growth and July new home sales will be released on Thursday.

Sept S&P 500 settled down 1.00 points to 665.70, Nikkei 225 futures fell 165.0 points to 20,780.0, Russell 2000 futures posted an 1.90 point gain to 336.20, NYSE Composite index fell 0.20 points to 357.20, Value Line rose 0.95 points to 624.75 and MidCap 400 rose 1.10 to 235.10.
